minutes.headline: Green Community Task Force agreed to draft a turnkey street light LED RFP with alternates, and set its next meeting for August 31.
minutes.summary: The task force welcomed a new member, approved prior minutes with the grant application attached, and discussed how to spend the Green Communities grant on converting town street lights to LED. They debated whether to pay for a separate design phase, a turnkey RFP, sample lights, wireless controls, metering, a maintenance contract and ordering of alternates. Members will review sample RFPs and mark them up before the next meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town was approved for a grant, of which a portion goes toward a hybrid plug-in police cruiser and a portion to administrative costs.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair wants a more proactive consultant than the regional planning agency for managing reports, and members discussed using the existing contact or another option.
The balance of the grant goes to street lights, previously voted as covering both a design phase and a build phase.
Members questioned whether the design phase is worth its cost and favored a turnkey design-build RFP.

budget_items.topic: Purchase of street lights from utility
budget_items.what_was_said: The town has agreed a price to buy the lights from the utility and is waiting for signing.
A large share of the current bill goes to maintenance under the utility.
A project manager previously quoted a general per-light figure, leaving funds left over.
Another town pays a truck-roll fee plus a per-additional-light fee; maintenance must be bid separately because the grant cannot pay for it.
Controls add a small per-fixture cost and lengthen the payback period.
A 2020 price for a four-foot pole with bracket was cited as not a significant difference.
Scrap value could be left with the bidder to lower bids, with the RFP explicit about who keeps the arms.

decisions.decision: A member will send out sample RFPs, bids and winning bids from other towns; each member will review and mark up for the next meeting.
Consensus leaning toward requesting full replacement of fixture arms as base scope, with limited alternates (controls/monitoring), to be drafted into the RFP.
Maintenance to be bid as a separate line item (about three years) from the installation, since grant funds cannot pay maintenance.

what_happened.line: The Green Community Task Force leaned toward a turnkey RFP for converting town street lights to LED, with full replacement of fixture arms as the base scope.
Controls and monitoring would be limited alternates in the RFP, which members agreed to draft.
Maintenance, about three years, is to be bid as a separate line item because grant funds cannot pay for maintenance.
A member will send sample RFPs and bids from other towns, and each member will mark them up before the next meeting.
The task force set its next meeting for August 31.

why_it_matters: The balance of the Green Communities grant is going to street lights, so the RFP's scope and alternates set how far that money stretches and what the town must fund itself, such as ongoing maintenance.
watch_next: Next task force meeting on August 31, where members bring marked-up sample RFPs.
